There is no direct relationship established between complex fractionated atrial electrograms (CFAEs) recorded during atrial fibrillation (AF) and sinus rhythm fractionation. In fact, studies suggest that CFAEs during AF may have little overlap with regions of sinus rhythm fractionation, indicating a potential difference in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

The majority of sinus rhythm fractionation occurs in regions with wave-front collision, whereas complex fractionated atrial electrograms are more closely associated with areas of atrial stretch and deformation. This suggests that CFAEs during AF may not be directly related to sinus rhythm fractionation, and therefore, do not provide a reliable indicator for this process.

It is essential to note that the absence of a clear relationship between these two phenomena does not rule out any potential mechanisms by which they could be linked in specific cases or populations. Further research is necessary to fully understand the nature of this association and its implications for diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation.
